title: Three months building an RTS - Zero coding
author: Disastrous-Dust-1449
selftext:
I've been a huge RTS fan for as long as I can remember. From Command & Conquer (Tiberian Dawn through to Tiberium Wars) to Sudden Strike (actually came 7th in a UK tournament when I was 15!) and Company of Heroes.

I'm a Product Manager by profession, so I'm used to working with software engineers, defining requirements and designing features. But I've got no programming experience myself.

Three months ago, I decided to see whether I could build the RTS game I've always wanted to play, using AI. I used, Claude and Chatgpt (working around weekly limits), Elevenlabs API for sound creation, Suno for music creation.

What started as an experiment has turned into a much bigger project than I ever expected.

So far, I've managed to build:

* A four-chapter single-player campaign, four missions per chapter, with a storyline following real historical events.
* 1v1 and 2v2 skirmish modes.
* Traditional RTS base building, resource management and unit production.
* Combat combining classic C&C gameplay with some Company of Heroes-style tactical elements.
* Those iconic C&C-style mid-game video cutscenes!

I've approached development much like I would manage a product at work: designing features, setting requirements, testing, finding issues and continually iterating. AI has allowed me to actually turn those ideas into a playable game.

It's certainly not been plain sailing. Some things that sound incredibly simple have taken countless iterations to get working properly, and I've learned a huge amount along the way.

I also hope I'm in the right place, the guys over at /realtimestrategy just loved my AI created RTS games post...

Happy to answer any questions about the development process, the tools I've used or the game itself!
